items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6898

SPONSOR: GOLDEN
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the general municipal law, in relation
to sick leave for officers and employees with a qualifying World Trade
Center condition; to amend the civil service law, in relation to the
review of certain claims; and to amend chapter 273 of the laws of 2017
amending the general municipal law, relating to granting sick leave for
officers and employees with a qualifying World Trade Center condition,
in relation to the reimbursement of any public authority or municipal
corporation of less than one million people for the cost of certain line
of duty sick leave

 
PURPOSE:

To provide the process for public authorities and municipal corporations
outside of New York City to obtain reimbursement for line of duty sick
leave granted to their employees.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section one of this bill amends section 92-d of the General Municipal
Law to provide a definition of the term "cost," as well as the procedure
for municipalities outside of New York City and public authorities to
receive reimbursement for the cost of line of duty sick leave.

Section two of this bill amends Civil Service Law section 6 by adding a
new subdivision 1-a. This new subdivision grants the State Civil Service
Commission with the power to review reimbursement claims submitted by
public authorities and municipal corporations outside New York City
pursuant to General Municipal Law section 92-d.

Section three of this bill amends Chapter 273 of the Laws of 2017 to
provide that reimbursement shall be made in accordance with General
Municipal Law section 92-d.

Section four of this bill provides that this act shall take effect imme-
diately and shall apply to all claims for reimbursement filed pursuant
to section one of this act.

 
CURRENT LAW:

Chapter 273 of the Laws of 2017 provided employees of public authorities
and municipalities outside of the City of New York who filed a notice of
participation in the World Trade Center rescue, recovery or cleanup
operations with the ability to receive line of duty sick leave when the
employee is on leave for doctor appointments or treatment of his or her
qualifying World Trade Center condition.  Public authorities and munici-
palities outside of the City of New York who provide line of duty sick
leave to employees can receive reimbursement for the cost of such sick
leave.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

While the Executive could administratively create a procedure for public
authorities and municipalities outside of the City of New York to
receive reimbursement for line of duty sick leave granted to employees,
such procedure would require coordination of multiple governmental enti-
ties, some of which are not part of the Executive Department. This bill
provides coordination among the governmental entities and creates a
clear procedure that can be easily followed by public authorities and
municipalities outside of the City of New York.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New Bill

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

Undetermined

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately and shall apply to all claims for
reimbursement filed pursuant to section one of this act.

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6898A

SPONSOR: GOLDEN
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the general municipal law and the
administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to sick leave
for officers and employees with a qualifying World Trade Center condi-
tion; to amend the civil service law, in relation to the review of
certain claims; and to amend chapter 273 of the laws of 2017 amending
the general municipal law, relating to granting sick leave for officers
and employees with a qualifying World Trade Center condition, in
relation to the reimbursement of any public authority or municipal
corporation in a city with a population of less than one million people
for the cost of certain line of duty sick leave

 
PURPOSE:

To clarify the eligibility for line of duty sick leave, to extend line
of duty sick leave to certain New York City employees, and to provide
the process for public authorities and municipal corporations outside of
New York City to obtain reimbursement for line of duty sick leave grant-
ed to their employees.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Sections one and two of this bill amend section 92-d of the General
Municipal Law to create 8 subdivisions. The original text of General
Municipal law section 92-d is subdivision 1. This subdivision has been
amended to clarify that an applicant for line of duty sick leave must
have filed and received approval for his or her notice of participation.
Additionally, this subdivision provides that no employee can receive
line of duty sick leave for any date prior to the date that he or she
engaged in rescue, recovery or cleanup operations. Finally, this subdi-
vision is amended to provide that nothing in the subdivision limits an
employer's power to discipline an employee or terminate an employee who
has not completed his or her probationary term, and to apply for ordi-
nary or accident disability retirement. This final provision currently
exists in the Administrative Code of the City of New York for the Police
Department and Fire Department when an employee is receiving line of
duty pay, which is the equivalent of the line of duty sick leave
provided by General Municipal Law section 92-d.

Section two of this bill adds subdivisions 2 through 8 to General Munic-
ipal Law section 92-d. New subdivision 2 extends the line of duty sick
leave benefits provided in subdivision 1 to New York City officers and
employees who do not currently have an equivalent benefit.

New subdivision three defines the term "cost" for the purpose of comput-
ing the cost to the employer who has provided line of duty sick leave to
an employee.

New subdivision four provides that any officer or employee who applies
for line of duty sick leave shall waive his or her rights under HIPAA
for the purpose of reviewing, processing and auditing his or her appli-
cation for line of duty sick leave. A waiver shall be filed with the
retirement system in which the application is a member.

New subdivision five provides that when an employer requests a copy of
an applicant's approved notice of participation from the retirement

system in which the applicant is a member, the retirement system shall
provide a verified copy of the approved notice of participation.

New subdivisions six, seven and eight provide the procedure for munici-
palities outside of New York City and public authorities to receive
reimbursement for the cost of line of duty sick leave.

Section three of this bill amends Civil Service Law section 6 by adding
a new subdivision 1-a. This new subdivision grants the State Civil
Service Commission with the power to review reimbursement claims submit-
ted by public authorities and municipal corporations outside New York
City pursuant to General Municipal Law section 92-d.

Section four of this bill amends Chapter 273 of the Laws of 2017 to
provide that reimbursement shall be made in accordance with General
Municipal Law section 92-d.

Section five of this bill amends the Administrative Code of the City of
New York by adding a new section 12-140 to codify the provisions in new
subdivision 2 of general Municipal Law section 92-d.

Section six of this bill requires the Commissioner of the Department of
Civil Service, in consultation with the Commissioner of the Department
of Taxation and Finance and the Comptroller, to provide guidance regard-
ing the implementation of General Municipal Law section 92-d. The guid-
ance shall include the tax treatment to officers and employees who
receive restored sick leave. If the guidance is issued as a regulation,
the Commissioner of the Department of Civil Service, this subdivision
provides the Commissioner with the ability to adopt the regulations on
an emergency basis.

Section seven of this bill provides that this act shall take effect
immediately; provided that section one of this act shall be deemed to
have been in full force and effect on the same date as chapter 273 of
the laws of 2017; and provided further that this act shall apply to all
claims for reimbursement filed pursuant to section 92-d of the general
municipal law, as amended by this act; and provided further, that any
officer or employee who is currently employed by a city with a popu-
lation of one million or more who has been diagnosed with a qualifying
World Trade Center condition and is using sick leave due to such condi-
tion shall receive a restoration of such sick leave retroactive to the
date such officer or employee was diagnosed with a qualifying World
Trade Center condition.

 
CURRENT LAW:

Chapter 273 of the Laws of 2017 provided employees of the State, public
authorities and municipalities outside of the City of New York who
engaged in the World Trade Center rescue, recovery or cleanup operations
with the ability to receive line of duty sick leave when the employee is
on leave for doctor appointments or treatment of his or her qualifying
World Trade Center condition. Public authorities and municipalities
outside of the City of New York who provide line of duty sick leave to
employees can receive reimbursement for the cost of such sick leave.

 
JUSTIFICATION:


This bill makes some necessary changes to Chapter 273 of the Laws of
2017 to provide clarification and the reimbursement procedure for local
governments and public authorities. This bill begins with the clarifica-
tion that line of duty sick leave is only available to applicants who
have filed and received approval of their notice of participation. This
bill also expands line of duty sick leave to officers and employees of
the City of New York who are not currently entitled to receive a benefit
similar to line of duty sick leave.  With this expansion, every public
officer or employee who, as a public officer or employee, engaged in
World Trade Center rescue, recovery or cleanup activities who receives
approval of his or her notice of participation is eligible to receive
line of duty sick leave if he or she becomes ill with a qualifying World
Trade Center condition. This expansion acknowledges that every public
employee who put his or her life on the line to help in our time of
crisis should receive the same benefits. In this instance, the benefit
is line of duty sick leave.

While the Executive could administratively create a procedure for public
authorities and municipalities outside of the City of New York to
receive reimbursement for line of duty sick leave granted to employees,
such procedure would require coordination of multiple governmental enti-
ties, some of which are not part of the Executive Department. This bill
provides coordination among the governmental entities and creates a
clear procedure that can be easily followed by public authorities and
municipalities outside of the City of New York. Should the City of New
York find that a similar procedure would be viable for use by the City,
the City can promulgate regulations to adopt a similar procedure.

We need to remember that there are 9/11 heroes who are struggling with
the onset and treatment of World Trade Center qualifying conditions
while trying to remain employed. This legislation helps these 9/11
heroes who are still able to work keep their jobs while they undergo
doctor's appointments and treatments for their World Trade Center quali-
fying condition.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New Bill

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

Undetermined

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately; provided that section one of
this act shall be deemed to have been in full force and effect on the
same date as chapter 273 of the laws of 2017; and provided further that
this act shall apply to all claims for reimbursement filed pursuant to
section 92-d of the general municipal law, as amended by this act; and
provided further, that any officer or employee who is currently employed
by a city with a population of one million or more who has been diag-
nosed with a qualifying World Trade Center condition and is using sick
leave due to such condition shall receive a restoration of such sick
leave retroactive to the date such officer or employee was diagnosed
with a qualifying World Trade Center condition.
